retrieved_contexts: ["Diabetes Also called: Diabetes mellitus, DM On this page Basics Summary Start Here Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Living With Related Issues Genetics See, Play and Learn Test Your Knowledge Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Reference Desk Find an Expert For You Women Older Adults Patient Handouts Summary What is diabetes? Diabetes, also known as diabetes mellitus, is a disease in which your blood glucose , or blood sugar, levels are too high. Glucose is your body's main source of energy. Your body can make glucose, but it also comes from the food you eat. Insulin is a hormone made by your pancreas. Insulin helps move glucose from your bloodstream into your cells, where it can be used for energy. If you have diabetes, your body can't make insulin, can't use insulin as well as it should, or both. Too much glucose stays in your blood and doesn't reach your cells. This can cause glucose levels to get too high. Over time, high blood glucose levels can lead to serious health conditions . But you can take steps to manage your diabetes and try to prevent these health problems. What are the types of diabetes? There are different types of diabetes: Type 1 diabetes . Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. But it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain. Not everyone infected with TB bacteria (germs) becomes sick. So, there are two types of TB conditions: Inactive (latent) TB infection , where the TB germs live in your body but don't make you sick. TB disease (active TB) where you get sick from the TB germs. TB disease can almost always be cured with antibiotics . But if it's not treated properly, it can be fatal. TB is found in the U.S., but it is more common in certain other countries. What causes tuberculosis (TB)? TB is caused by bacteria (germs) called Mycobacterium tuberculosis . The germs spread from person to person through the air. People who have TB disease in their throat or lungs spread the germs in the air when they cough, sneeze, talk, or sing. If you breathe in the air that has the germs, you can get TB. TB is not spread by touching, kissing, or sharing food or dishes. You're more likely to catch TB from people you live or work with than from people you see for shorter amounts of time. Who is more likely to get infected with tuberculosis (TB) germs? Anyone who is near a person with TB disease can get infected with the germs. You are more likely to be near someone with TB disease if you: Were born in or often travel to countries where TB disease is common Are a health care worker Work or live in a place where TB is more common, such as shelters for people without homes, jails, and nursing homes Who is more likely to develop TB disease? Certain people are more likely to get sick with TB disease after they get infected. There are many different types of heart disease. Some you may be born with, called congenital heart disease . Other types develop during your lifetime. Cancer is not just one disease but many diseases. Cancer begins in your cells, which are the building blocks of your body. Usually, your body forms new cells as needed, replacing old cells that die. Sometimes this process goes wrong. New cells grow even when you don't need them, and old cells don't die when they should. These extra cells can form a mass called a tumor. Tumors can be benign or malignant. Benign tumors aren't cancer, while malignant ones are. Cells from malignant tumors can invade nearby tissues. Symptoms and treatment depend on the type of cancer and how advanced it is. What are the types of cancer? There are more than 100 different types of cancer. retrieved_contexts: ["Tuberculosis Also called: TB On this page Basics Summary Start Here Symptoms Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Related Issues Specifics See, Play and Learn No links available Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Reference Desk Find an Expert For You Children Women Patient Handouts Summary What is tuberculosis (TB)? Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. But it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain. Not everyone infected with TB bacteria (germs) becomes sick. So, there are two types of TB conditions: Inactive (latent) TB infection , where the TB germs live in your body but don't make you sick. TB disease (active TB) where you get sick from the TB germs. TB disease can almost always be cured with antibiotics . But if it's not treated properly, it can be fatal. TB is found in the U.S., but it is more common in certain other countries. What causes tuberculosis (TB)? TB is caused by bacteria (germs) called Mycobacterium tuberculosis . The germs spread from person to person through the air. People who have TB disease in their throat or lungs spread the germs in the air when they cough, sneeze, talk, or sing. If you breathe in the air that has the germs, you can get TB. TB is not spread by touching, kissing, or sharing food or dishes. Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs. But it can also attack other parts of the body, including the kidneys, spine, and brain. Not everyone infected with TB bacteria (germs) becomes sick. So, there are two types of TB conditions: Inactive (latent) TB infection , where the TB germs live in your body but don't make you sick. TB is found in the U.S., but it is more common in certain other countries. What causes tuberculosis (TB)? TB is caused by bacteria (germs) called Mycobacterium tuberculosis . The germs spread from person to person through the air. People who have TB disease in their throat or lungs spread the germs in the air when they cough, sneeze, talk, or sing. retrieved_contexts: ["Cancer Also called: Carcinoma, Malignancy, Neoplasms, Tumor On this page Basics Summary Start Here Diagnosis and Tests Prevention and Risk Factors Treatments and Therapies Learn More Living With Related Issues Specifics Genetics See, Play and Learn Videos and Tutorials Research Statistics and Research Clinical Trials Journal Articles Resources Reference Desk Find an Expert For You Children Teenagers Men Women Patient Handouts Summary What is cancer? Cancer is not just one disease but many diseases. Cancer begins in your cells, which are the building blocks of your body. Usually, your body forms new cells as needed, replacing old cells that die. Sometimes this process goes wrong. New cells grow even when you don't need them, and old cells don't die when they should. These extra cells can form a mass called a tumor. Tumors can be benign or malignant. Benign tumors aren't cancer, while malignant ones are. Cells from malignant tumors can invade nearby tissues. They can also break away and spread to other parts of your body. The spread of cancer from one part of the body to another is called metastasis. Symptoms and treatment depend on the type of cancer and how advanced it is. What are the types of cancer? There are more than 100 different types of cancer. Cancer can start almost anywhere in your body. Most cancers are named for where they start. For example, lung cancer starts in the lung, and breast cancer starts in the breast. Diabetes, also known as diabetes mellitus, is a disease in which your blood glucose , or blood sugar, levels are too high. Glucose is your body's main source of energy. Your body can make glucose, but it also comes from the food you eat. Insulin is a hormone made by your pancreas. Insulin helps move glucose from your bloodstream into your cells, where it can be used for energy. If you have diabetes, your body can't make insulin, can't use insulin as well as it should, or both. Too much glucose stays in your blood and doesn't reach your cells. This can cause glucose levels to get too high. Over time, high blood glucose levels can lead to serious health conditions . But you can take steps to manage your diabetes and try to prevent these health problems. What are the types of diabetes? There are different types of diabetes: Type 1 diabetes . If you have type 1 diabetes, your body makes little or no insulin. It happens when your immune system attacks and destroys the cells that produce insulin. Type 2 diabetes . This is the most common form of diabetes. If you have type 2 diabetes, your body may still be able to make insulin, but your cells don't respond well to insulin. They can't easily take up enough glucose from your blood. Gestational diabetes . This is a form of diabetes that develops during pregnancy. Of course. It's important to understand the difference between these two types of arthritis, as their causes and treatments are very different. Let's explain it in a simple way.

Think of your body's defense system, the immune system, as an army that protects you from invaders like germs (bacteria and viruses).

### Infectious Arthritis (The "Invader" Arthritis)

*   **What it is:** This is like a direct infection inside your joint.
*   **The Cause:** A germ, such as bacteria or a virus, enters your joint and starts to multiply. This could happen from an infection elsewhere in your body (like a skin infection or a urinary tract infection) that spreads to the joint, or sometimes from an injury.
*   **The Analogy:** Imagine an enemy army (the germ) has invaded your castle (the joint). Your body's army (the immune system) rushes to the joint to fight the enemy. The battle itself causes a lot of damage, leading to sudden pain, swelling, redness, and heat in the joint.
*   **The Treatment:** The main goal is to get rid of the invading germ. This is usually done with strong antibiotics or antiviral medicines.

### Autoimmune Arthritis (The "Mistaken Identity" Arthritis)

*   **What it is:** This is a condition where your body's own defense system mistakenly attacks your healthy tissues, including your joints.
*   **The Cause:** For reasons that are not fully understood, the immune system gets confused and thinks your own joints are foreign invaders. It launches an attack against them.
*   **The Analogy:** Think of your immune system's army as having friendly fire. Instead of protecting the castle, the soldiers start attacking the castle walls and towers (the joints) by mistake. This "friendly fire" causes chronic inflammation, pain, stiffness, and can lead to joint damage over time.
*   **The Treatment:** Since there is no external germ to fight, the treatment focuses on calming down the overactive immune system so it stops attacking the joints. This is done with medicines that suppress the immune system (immunosuppressants) or reduce inflammation.

### Summary of Key Differences

| Feature | Infectious Arthritis | Autoimmune Arthritis |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cause** | An external germ (bacteria/virus) infects the joint. | The body's own immune system mistakenly attacks the joints. |
| **Onset** | Often sudden and acute. | Often gradual and chronic (long-lasting). |
| **Primary Treatment** | Antibiotics or antivirals to kill the germ. | Medicines to calm the immune system and reduce inflammation. |

In short, with infectious arthritis, the problem is an **outside enemy**. With autoimmune arthritis, the problem is an **inside mistake**.

It is very important to see a doctor for a correct diagnosis, as the treatment for one is not effective for the other.

**General Knowledge:**

A stroke is a medical emergency that occurs when blood flow to an area of the brain is interrupted. This can happen either because a blood vessel supplying the brain is blocked by a clot (ischemic stroke) or because a blood vessel ruptures and bleeds into the brain (hemorrhagic stroke).

A stroke is dangerous because brain cells are deprived of oxygen and nutrients and begin to die within minutes. This cell death can lead to the loss of functions controlled by that part of the brain, such as movement, speech, and memory. The effects can be permanent, causing long-term disability, paralysis, or even death. The severity of the damage depends on the location of the stroke and how quickly the person receives medical treatment.

Asthma is a chronic (long-term) lung disease. It affects your airways, the tubes that carry air in and out of your lungs. When you have asthma, your airways can become inflamed and narrowed. Allergens are substances that cause an allergic reaction. They can include Dust mites Mold Pets Pollen from grass, trees, and weeds Waste from pests such as cockroaches and mice Nonallergic asthma is caused by triggers that are not allergens, such as Breathing in cold air Certain medicines Household chemicals Infections such as colds and the flu Outdoor air pollution Tobacco smoke Occupational asthma is caused by breathing in chemicals or industrial dusts at work Exercise-induced asthma happens during physical exercise, especially when the air is dry Asthma triggers may be different for each person and can change over time. ---

**General Knowledge:**

The treatments for ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes are fundamentally different because they address opposite problems: a blockage versus a bleed.

*   **Ischemic Stroke Treatment:** The goal is to restore blood flow to the brain by dissolving or removing the clot.
    *   **Thrombolysis:** "Clot-busting" drugs, such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), are administered intravenously to dissolve the clot. This must be given within a specific time window (typically 3 to 4.5 hours from symptom onset).
    *   **Mechanical Thrombectomy:** A minimally invasive procedure where a catheter is used to physically remove the clot from the blocked artery.

*   **Hemorrhagic Stroke Treatment:** The goal is to stop the bleeding, reduce pressure on the brain, and prevent further bleeding.
    *   **Blood Pressure Control:** Medications are used to lower blood pressure and reduce the strain on the weakened blood vessel.
    *   **Reversing Anticoagulants:** If the patient is on blood thinners (like warfarin or apixaban), specific medications or treatments are given to reverse their effects.
    *   **Surgical Intervention:** In some cases, surgery may be needed to repair the ruptured blood vessel (e.g., clipping or coiling an aneurysm) or to remove the accumulated blood (hematoma) to relieve pressure on the brain.

The most critical first step in any stroke case is to determine whether it is ischemic or hemorrhagic, as giving a clot-busting drug to a patient with a hemorrhagic stroke would be fatal.

If you feel pain and stiffness in your body or have trouble moving around, you might have arthritis. Any disorder that affects the joints is often called arthritis. Joints are places where two bones meet, such as your elbow or knee. Most types of arthritis can cause joint pain and inflammation (swelling). Over time, a swollen joint can become severely damaged. Some kinds of arthritis can also cause problems in your organs, such as your eyes or skin. Treatment will depend on the type of arthritis you have. What are the types of arthritis? Common types of arthritis include: Osteoarthritis is the most common type of arthritis. It's often related to aging or injury. सौम्य (benign) और घातक (malignant) ट्यूमर के बीच मुख्य अंतर निम्नलिखित हैं:

*   **आक्रमण (Invasion):** सौम्य ट्यूमर आसपास के ऊतकों (tissues) पर आक्रमण नहीं करते हैं। घातक ट्यूमर आसपास के ऊतकों पर आक्रमण करते हैं और उन्हें नष्ट कर देते हैं।
*   **पुनरावृत्ति:** सौम्य ट्यूमर को शल्य चिकित्सा (सर्जरी) द्वारा हटाने के बाद उनके वापस आने की संभावना कम होती है। घातक ट्यूमर के वापस आने की संभावना अधिक होती है क्योंकि उनके सूक्ष्म, फैलते हुए कोशिका समूह पीछे छूट सकते हैं।
*   **जीवन के लिए खतरा:** सौम्य ट्यूमर सामान्यतः जीवन के लिए खतरा नहीं होते हैं। घातक ट्यूमर जीवन के लिए खतरा हो सकते हैं और कैंसर का एक रूप हैं।

Travelers who have not been previously exposed to the parasite do not have natural immunity, making them highly susceptible to infection. Preventive medicines work to kill the parasite in the body before it can cause illness, thus protecting the traveler from contracting malaria during and after their trip. The specific medication recommended depends on the destination country, the traveler's health status, and potential drug interactions.

Juvenile arthritis is a type of arthritis that happens in children. Infectious arthritis is an infection that has spread from another part of your body to the joint. Reactive arthritis is one type.
